title: Rabbi David Tawil: Yehoshua Chapter 4- "Rocks and Memory"

summary: Rabbi Tawil explores the significance of the 12 stones erected by Yehoshua after the Jewish people crossed the Jordan River. He discusses how these monuments serve as a tool for unity, a means of transmitting history from father to son, and a symbol of the partnership between human initiative and the miracles of Hashem. The class contrasts this natural stone monument with the man-made bricks of Egypt to highlight the importance of Jewish memory and continuity.
questions: Why did Yehoshua command the people to take stones from the Jordan River?
What is the difference between the stones used for the monument and the bricks made in Egypt?
How do these stones serve as a tool for teaching the next generation?
Why is it important for the Jewish people to memorialize both positive and negative events?
What does the act of placing stones in the river signify about our partnership with Hashem?
